subject: Payment waterfall, regional tax split & invoice cadence — Order Form v3
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@novonexus.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: AP Team <ap@novonexus.com>, Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@novonexus.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form questions — invoicing cadence + tax allocation

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for sending over Order Form v3. Our procurement team ran the commercial table and has three items we need clarity on before we loop in legal: 

1) Waterfall / invoice cadence: The SOW references an annual commit but our finance org needs quarterly invoices tied to milestone consumption (quarterly true-ups). Can you confirm whether Redwood can support: initial invoice at signature (25%), quarterly consumption invoices, and a year-end true-up?

2) Credits / outage credits: We need a clear line saying credits are applied as a cash credit on the next invoice vs. a separate credit memo.

3) Tax / withholding: NovoNexus is headquartered in the US but has EU subsidiaries. We need the invoice tax residency to be explicit — Redwood should invoice US entity for US spend and issue separate invoices for EU spend (if any), or confirm Redwood will accept customer tax-exemption evidence.

Attaching a short spreadsheet with what our AP prefers. Can you please route to your billing and legal teams and let us know?

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Head of Procurement — NovoNexus

(Attachment: Novo_AP_Preferences.csv)

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@novonexus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence + tax allocation

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear summary and the sheet. Forwarding to our billing and finance owners below; quick answers up front so you have something to share with legal: 

- Invoice cadence: yes, Redwood can support an initial prepayment at signature (25%), then quarterly invoices for consumption with a year-end true-up. We propose: initial invoice on signature, Q1/Q2/Q3 invoices at the start of each quarter (forecasted consumption), and Q4 true-up based on actuals.

- Credits: we'll apply service credits as a credit line on the subsequent invoice and include a clear credit memo number for audit.

- Tax split: we can issue region-specific invoices if the usage is tied to different legal entities — otherwise we need tax-exemption evidence from the customer. If NovoNexus will centralize payment through the US entity but require EU invoices, we'll need an assertion of the EU spend allocation (CSV or SFTP report).

Ben / Rishi / Camila — please see Priya's ask and the attached Novo_AP_Preferences.csv. Can you review the proposed waterfall and confirm any changes needed to the Order Form commercial language (pricing schedule, minimum commit implications for quarterly true-ups, and tax evidence requirements)?

Action items I expect: 
- Ben: propose redline language for the "Invoices and Payment" clause and credit handling.
- Rishi: confirm VAT/EU invoice process and required tax evidence (EU VAT number, W-8/W-9 equivalents).
- Camila: confirm how minimum commit / refunds interact with quarterly true-ups and whether we need to convert commits to a prorated schedule for the first partial year.

I'll pull together a redlined Order Form after your inputs and share a DocuSign-ready version.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(Attachment: Novo_AP_Preferences.csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence + tax allocation

Rohan / team — I reviewed Priya's ask and sketched redline suggestions below (high level):

1) Invoices and Payment: Add explicit waterfall language: 
   - 25% due on execution (non-refundable credit to be applied to invoices)
   - Quarterly invoices issued net 30, representing forecasted consumption; actual usage to be reconciled at year-end
   - Any underpayment vs minimum commit remains due at reconciliation; any overpayment will be applied as a credit against the next invoice or refunded at Redwood's discretion if requested within 90 days

2) Credits / Outages: Add clause: service credits for SLA violations will be applied as an invoice credit and reflected on the subsequent billing statement with a unique credit memo id. No cash refunds unless explicitly approved by Redwood Finance (exec exception).

3) Minimum commit phrasing: Make sure minimum commit is defined as an annual dollar commitment; quarterly invoices are estimates and do not relieve the customer of the annual minimum. For the first partial year, propose pro-rataing the annual commit to the number of remaining months.

4) Tax / Withholding: Redwood will invoice the entity identified on the Order Form. If customer requests multi-entity invoicing, NovoNexus must provide a mapping (CSV) of entity-to-usage by month and valid tax IDs. Otherwise Redwood will issue a single invoice to the payer entity and customer is responsible for internal allocation and any withholding taxes.

I attached a sample Payment-Waterfall.xlsx that maps the scheduled invoices and reconciliation rows. If legal prefers different wording I can make edits — but the above is what Finance needs to reconcile AR (Rishi: any flagged items?).

- Ben
Sales Ops — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: Payment-Waterfall.xlsx)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence + tax allocation

Thanks Ben — this looks good. A couple of finance clarifications: 

- VAT / EU: If NovoNexus wants EU-level invoices that include VAT, we need the EU entity VAT number and an authorized contact for that entity. We can generate separate invoices but we will require a monthly usage split file (CSV) to tie charges to the appropriate legal entity prior to invoice generation.

- WHT: For jurisdictions with withholding, customer must provide a certificate of residency or treaty claim prior to Redwood issuing a net-of-withholding invoice. Without that, Redwood will invoice gross and customer is responsible for withholding and any related remittance.

- Credits: Finance prefers the credit-memo-on-next-invoice model (as Ben suggested). For audit, include a credit_memo_id in the invoice XML such that our AR system can reconcile.

- PO & Net Terms: If NovoNexus requires a PO on each invoice, we'll accept PO numbers but net 30 remains the standard. If they want Net 45 or Net 60, that should be an explicit commercial term tied to the order and may impact the discount / prepayment structuring.

I'll flag that refunds are handled as exceptions — we prefer credits.

Rishi
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@novonexus.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.inference.com>, AP Team <ap@novonexus.com>
Date: Mon, 23 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoicing cadence + tax allocation

Priya — thanks for the patience while we coordinated internally. Summary and next steps below: 

Summary of agreed commercial approach (to include in Order Form v3 redline):
- Payment waterfall: 25% due at signature (applied as a non-refundable credit), quarterly invoices for forecasted consumption, year-end true-up to reconcile to annual minimum commit.
- Minimum commit: defined as annual $ commitment; first year will be prorated if mid-year start. Underpayments at true-up are invoiced immediately; overpayments will be applied as credits to the next invoice unless NovoNexus requests a refund within 90 days.
- Credits: SLA credits applied as invoice credits (credit memo ID), shown on subsequent invoice. Cash refunds only via finance exception.
- Tax & invoicing: Redwood will invoice the legal entity listed on the Order Form. If multi-entity invoicing is required, NovoNexus to provide monthly usage mapping and tax IDs for each entity before go-live; otherwise customer handles internal allocation and any withholding.
- PO & terms: Redwood accepts PO numbers but standard terms are Net 30. Any requests for Net 45/60 to be documented in the order and may impact commercial concessions.

Attachments / next artifacts: I've attached a redlined OrderForm-v3-redlines.docx and the Payment-Waterfall.xlsx for your review. If the above looks good, please confirm and we will route the redline to legal for final wording and prepare a DocuSign packet.

Priya — can you confirm by EOD Wed 26 May whether NovoNexus will: (a) accept the single-payer US invoicing model and handle internal allocations, or (b) provide a mapping and tax evidence for multi-entity invoicing?

Thanks all — looping in legal once we have NovoNexus confirmation.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

redwood.inference.com
